entries.old_text: OVAL_RECORD: The phrase was used as permission: he is the danger, so the law may be broken to stop him. That is not what it means. Holmes wrote it in Schenck v. United States (1919). Brandenburg v. Ohio (1969) replaced it: the government may punish speech only if it is intended to produce imminent lawless action and likely to produce it. It is a limit on the state. It is not a finding that a president may be FISA’d sloppily, impeached on a clipped tape, or indicted on a theory timed to an election. Repeating the words on television does not suspend the Constitution.
